script:
These humanoids learn to walk before touching the real world.
And the crazy part is, years of practice take just a few hours.
This is Figure's training ground for Figure 02.
Inside one physics simulator, thousands of virtual robots learn at once.
It's like a video game with infinite lives, except the high score is walking.
The AI tries a movement, gets rewarded for copying a human gait, then adjusts and tries again.
But here's the hardest part.
A simulated robot only approximates a real one.
So Figure makes the simulation messy.
Every robot gets different physical properties and faces changing terrain, slips and shoves.
The AI can't memorize one perfect world.
It has to learn walking that works outside it.
And it works.
The same controller transferred to real robots with no extra tuning.
Figure even ran it on 10 robots with zero changes.
Soon, a robot's first real step could have years of practice behind it.
Follow for more tech, AI and robotics stories.
